newsitem.title: JAPAN: 'Mr Yen' takes a holiday, sets off mad scramble.
newsitem.headline: 'Mr Yen' takes a holiday, sets off mad scramble.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, if you read this, call your office.

Markets in Tokyo were set abuzz on Thursday when rumours emerged that the powerful Japanese Finance Ministry official, who was supposedly on a long-overdue holiday, was seen in town and likely to make comments about Japan's phenomenally low interest rates.
The rumours set off a mad scramble in search of the elusive official, dubbed "Mr Yen" by market pundits for his ability to roil the markets with a few choice words.
Japanese government bond prices shot up in the morning on the talk, only to recede later on repeated denials from his office.
Calls to the ministry were met by exasperated officials who insisted that Sakakibara would not be seen or heard until next Tuesday.
"He is out of Japan on holiday at a place far from work, and he is not in such places as New York, Washington or Europe," a source close to the ministry said.
For market players still intent on looking for the official, that would leave Africa, the Middle East and other parts of the Asia Pacific as other possible getaways.
